chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Asim from Muhammad ibn Qays said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled in a will witnessed only by a woman that the testimony of a woman is valid for one-quarter of the will if she is Muslim and not doubtful in her religion.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's testimony in witnessing a will according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights a specific juristic ruling by Imam Ali (AS) regarding the admissibility of a single woman's testimony in wills, limiting its scope to one-quarter of the estate. The condition of being 'non-doubtful in faith' (ghayr muribah) underscores the Shia emphasis on both religious integrity and legal reliability in witness selection. This ruling reflects the practical application of Quranic principles of testimony within the early Islamic community's legal framework.
